original_post_text:
𝐇𝐞 𝐖𝐨𝐧 $𝟏𝟒𝟑,𝟎𝟎𝟎 𝐚𝐭 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐋𝐨𝐝𝐠𝐞. 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐧 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐖𝐞𝐫𝐞 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐝𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐍𝐞𝐱𝐭 𝐃𝐚𝐲.

I saw a story post from 23-year-old Harvey Castro saying he was looking forward to getting back to grinding since the Lodge incident. That caught my attention.

Harvey Castro finished 2nd in the Lodge Championship Series Main Event on March 9th, 2026. His prize? $143,336.
He was paid zero dollars.

His check was still at the Lodge when the raid happened that morning. The timing couldn't have been worse.

I reached out to Harvey for a statement and he was kind enough to speak with The Sham Report.

In his own words:

"They told me they would mail me the check. The day later they were raided. Doug has told me he will pay should it come to that. But it sucks right now man."

Ever since Harvey came into the DFW poker scene it's been hard not to like this kid. He's from Flower Mound, Texas. Started out playing weekly tournaments at Texas Card House Dallas and Shuffle 214. Those rooms were his training ground. Now he has over $1,850,000 in live tournament earnings at 23 years old.

Almost $2 million. At 23. And he's probably one of the most humble players on the circuit.

We're rooting for you Harvey. You earned that money at the table. Hopefully the Lodge makes it right.

Click Like to show some love for one of Texas's brightest poker stars.

#HarveyCastro #TheLodge #TexasPoker #TheShamReport
expanded_title: He Won $143,000 at The Lodge. Then They Were Raided the Next Day: Harvey Castro Speaks to The Sham Report

expanded_body:
Originally posted April 21, 2026.

He won $143,000 at The Lodge. Then they were raided the next day.

I saw a story post from 23-year-old Harvey Castro saying he was looking forward to getting back to grinding since The Lodge incident. That caught my attention.

Harvey Castro finished second in the Lodge Championship Series Main Event on March 9, 2026. His prize? $143,336.

At the time of the raid, he had been paid zero dollars. His check was still at The Lodge when agents walked in that Tuesday morning, March 10. The timing couldn't have been worse.

I reached out to Harvey for a statement, and he was kind enough to speak directly with The Sham Report. In his own words:

"They told me they would mail me the check. The day later they were raided. Doug has told me he will pay should it come to that. But it sucks right now man."

Ever since Harvey came into the DFW poker scene, it's been hard not to like this kid. He's from Flower Mound, Texas, and started out playing weekly tournaments at Texas Card House Dallas and Shuffle 214. Those rooms were his training ground. Now he has over $1,850,000 in live tournament earnings at 23 years old.

Almost $2 million at 23 — and he's probably one of the most humble players on the circuit.

We're rooting for you, Harvey. You earned that money at the table.

— Sham

fact_verification_flags.claim: Harvey Castro finished 2nd in the Lodge Championship Series Main Event on March 9, 2026 for $143,336 and provided a direct statement to The Sham Report regarding his unpaid check following the March 10 raid
fact_verification_flags.note: Direct interview by Shomari Williams with Harvey Castro, accompanied by LCS Final Table broadcast screenshot (images/2026-04-21_1.jpg).

outdated_info_flags.original_statement: He was paid zero dollars. His check was still at the Lodge when the raid happened that morning.
outdated_info_flags.current_status: On April 28, 2026, a Williamson County grand jury returned a no-bill declining charges, and The Lodge reopened in May 2026
outdated_info_flags.editorial_note: Describes the status of Castro's payout check on April 21, 2026 while The Lodge's accounts were frozen prior to the April 28 grand jury no-bill.
